title: wsutil: Read the Linux socket tables through netlink
description:
The first of the two Linux follow-ups mentioned in !26518 in reply to @AndersBroman's question about hosts with very many sockets. It only touches the Linux backend of `wsutil/process_lookup.h` (!26493).

The backend read the sockets from `/proc/net/{tcp,udp}{,6}`. The kernel takes a long time to produce those text tables when there are many sockets. This reads them through a `NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG` socket instead, as `ss` does: one `inet_diag_req_v2` dump per address family and protocol, from which the addresses, ports and inode of each socket are taken. Which processes have each inode open still comes from `/proc/<pid>/fd`.

Measured in the CI container with 50,000 UDP sockets held by 5 processes, per refresh:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| refresh | 9 to 10.5 s | 0.7 to 0.9 s |

Of what remains, the four netlink dumps are 0.10 to 0.16 s, measured separately; the rest is the scan of `/proc/<pid>/fd` (50,000 readlink calls, 0.55 to 0.8 s), which is the same as before.

- No privilege is needed, and the sockets are those of the caller's network namespace, as before. No new dependency: the uapi headers, no libnl.
- TIME_WAIT sockets, which nobody has open, are left out of the request rather than skipped afterwards.
- Messages that do not come from the kernel, or that answer an earlier request, are ignored.
- Fallback: if the netlink socket can't be created, or a request fails (a kernel without the `inet_diag` module of a protocol, a sandbox that refuses netlink), `/proc/net` is read instead from then on, with the existing parser. IPv6 is still only asked for when `/proc/net/tcp6` exists.

Tests: the existing `test_wsutil` process lookup tests now run through netlink (checked with strace: four dumps per refresh, no `/proc/net` reads) and pass with gcc, and with clang and ASan. Both fallbacks were exercised with LD_PRELOAD shims, one refusing the `NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG` socket and one failing the second dump request: in both cases a sample of 516 of the 50,000 sockets is found, as through netlink. Together with !26518, its capture tests pass as a user and as root.
